name: Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 + CSSF Regulation 12-02
reference: Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) + CSSF Reg 12-02 + Grand-Ducal Reg 1 Feb 2010
supervisor: CSSF + CAA + AED + Bar Council + Notarial Chamber + ICCC

articles.title: Designated persons
articles.requirement: Designated persons include: credit institutions; investment firms; payment + e-money institutions; UCITS ManCos + AIFMs (managing AIFs that are marketed); insurance undertakings + intermediaries (life); other CSSF + CAA supervised PSF; lawyers + notaries (when carrying out specified financial / property / corporate transactions); accountants + auditors + tax advisers; real estate agents; trust + company service providers; high-value-goods dealers (≥ €10,000); art-market participants; CASPs.

articles.title: Risk-based approach + entity-wide assessment
articles.requirement: Designated persons must conduct + maintain a documented entity-wide ML/TF risk assessment, refreshed at least annually + on material change. Risk factors: customer, geographic, product/service, distribution channel, new technologies. Calibrates the intensity of all other AML obligations.

articles.title: CDD application
articles.requirement: CDD applied: at establishment of a business relationship; for occasional transactions of €15,000+ (or €1,000+ for wire transfers); on suspicion of ML/TF irrespective of any threshold; where there are doubts about the veracity / adequacy of previously obtained CDD information.

articles.title: CDD measures
articles.requirement: Identify + verify the customer using documents / data / information from reliable + independent sources; identify the beneficial owner + take reasonable measures to verify (25% threshold + senior-managing-official fallback); obtain information on purpose + intended nature of the relationship; conduct ongoing monitoring (transaction scrutiny + record refresh).

articles.title: Enhanced due diligence
articles.requirement: EDD required for: high-risk third countries; cross-border correspondent relationships; PEPs (domestic + foreign + IO); complex / unusual / large transactions with no apparent economic purpose; situations representing higher risk per the entity's risk assessment. Senior-management approval; source-of-wealth + source-of-funds; enhanced ongoing monitoring.

articles.title: Simplified due diligence
articles.requirement: Simplified CDD permitted only for lower-risk situations identified by the entity's risk assessment + supported by the SNRA / NRA. Does not exempt from any obligation; reduces intensity (e.g. delayed verification within strict limits).

articles.title: Suspicious-transaction reporting (déclaration de soupçon)
articles.requirement: Designated persons file SARs to the CRF without delay where they know, suspect or have reasonable grounds to suspect ML/TF or that funds are connected to a criminal organisation. Tipping-off prohibition. Statutory immunity for good-faith reporters. Internal escalation procedures required.

articles.title: Internal organisation
articles.requirement: Designated persons must implement internal policies, controls + procedures proportionate to size + risk: governance + accountability arrangements (RC + RR); CDD procedures; reliance on third parties; transaction monitoring; reporting; record retention (≥ 5 years); staff vetting + training; independent audit + review.

articles.title: RC + RR roles (CSSF Regulation 12-02)
articles.requirement: Financial-sector designated persons must appoint a Responsable du Contrôle du respect des obligations professionnelles (RC) — operational AML compliance officer at senior management level — and a Responsable du Respect des obligations professionnelles (RR) — at board / executive-committee level with overall accountability. Both subject to CSSF assessment + must have sufficient seniority + independence + resources.

articles.title: Sanctions
articles.requirement: Administrative + criminal sanctions: criminal — up to 5 years' imprisonment for individuals + significant fines; administrative — CSSF + supervisory authorities may impose monetary penalties, prohibitions on holding management functions, withdrawal of authorisation; reputational impact through CSSF public notices (Article 25 enforcement notices).
